app.title: Atalaia · Game control
app.reconnecting: No connection to the field controller. Reconnecting…

login.intro: The organisers' console, served by the field controller.

alerts.start_forced: Game started without a box for: {roles}

game.title: Game
game.name: Game name
game.teams_hint: Separated by commas, in the order of the buttons (for example: red, blue).
game.modifiers_hint: They run alongside the mode on its boxes (for example keypad codes).
game.wait_gm: The organisers have not created a game yet.
game.standby_notice: This controller is on standby in this game: it follows the main controller and only takes charge if promoted.
game.not_leader: This controller is not in charge of the game. To run it from here, promote it in the Controller tab.
game.confirm_start_pending: {n} declared replica(s) not chronographed yet. Start anyway?
game.squads_hint: 0 = no squads (small games: teams only). In a milsim or a big game each team splits into squads.
game.disclosure: Who a squad's objectives go to
game.disclosure_hint: A squad only ever gets its active objective; the next is revealed when it is completed. With the squad leader only, the members are told that their leader has new orders. If the leader is absent, nobody in the squad gets the objective: choose every member then.
game.role_packages: Props with a role of their own
game.role_packages_hint: Boxes and phones given their role run only them, next to the mode's boxes (for example medic kits).
game.missing_roles: Start waits for a box (or a linked phone) for: {roles}. Invite boxes, or start anyway.

start_warnings.last: Only {have} × {role} joined and {param} is {value}: the countdown can run from the start.

game.settings_hint: Set when the game was created; to change them, end this game and create another one.
game.key_lost_notice: This controller restarted without the game's key (persist_game_key was off): the game can only be ended. Ending it tells its boxes over the field radio, sealed with the field join key, and they leave the game.
game.confirm_end_key_lost: End the game and tell its boxes over the field radio?
game.over_told: The game's boxes were told over the field radio that it is over.
game.over_not_told: The boxes could not be told over the radio ({why}): restart each box, or join it to the next game with a card.

controller.title: Field controller
controller.confirm_promote: This controller will take charge of the game. Continue?
controller.promote_hint: Promote a standby controller when the main one stops answering (manual failover).
controller.missing_areas: This controller does not serve these parts of the console yet, so they are hidden: {areas}.

score.title: Score
score.timeline: Score over time since the console opened

events.medic_heal: {player} was healed (heals left in the kit: {remaining}; heals in this game: {used})
events.hacking_solved_code: {team} solved a hacking terminal ({puzzle}) and got the code {code}
events.progressive_activated: Box {zone} is active now (number {step}): the only one that can be captured
events.scenario_objective_revealed_all: The objective {objective} is revealed to every team
events.scenario_objective_revealed_all_hidden: An objective is revealed to every team
events.game_end_by: The game ended: ended by box {by}

nodes.title: Boxes
nodes.none: No boxes in this game yet.
nodes.name: Name
nodes.conflict: Two boxes share node {node}: one join was used on two boxes, and they use the same radio nonces. Take one of them out of the game and join it again with a new join (Join).

field.title: Field
field.bad_type: The field image must be PNG, JPEG or WebP.
field.no_image: No field image: the boxes are shown on a grid.
field.drag_hint: Drag the boxes to where they are on the field.

georef.title: Map position (ATAK)
georef.intro: Give two opposite corners of the field image their latitude and longitude, copied from a map app as "latitude, longitude": any two (top-left and bottom-right, or bottom-left and top-right); the console works out which is which. The image must have north at the top.
georef.none: The image has no map position yet: the ATAK feed sends no boxes.
georef.points: Set with {n} control points through the API (they agree to {residual} m). Saving two corners replaces them.
georef.privacy: The ATAK feed sends the boxes and the extraction zone to anyone on the field Wi-Fi; player positions never go there, only to the staff devices set in controller.toml.
georef.atak_on: ATAK feed: on, {markers} markers on the map, {sent} messages sent.

levels.hint_off: Tick it if the field is a building with several floors: each floor has its own plan and each box sits on its floor.
levels.hint_on: Each level has its own floor plan. Choose the level with the tabs above the plan. For a basement, give a level that name.
levels.name: Name of level {n}
levels.no_image: {name} has no plan yet: the boxes on this level are shown on a grid.
levels.confirm_off: Turn levels off? Only the plan of {ground} stays in use, as the field image, and every box shows on it. The other plans, the names and each box's level are kept and come back if you turn levels on again.
levels.confirm_fewer: With fewer levels, the plans of {names} are deleted, with their map features, and the boxes on those levels move to {ground}. Go on?
levels.georef_shared: This level uses the map position of {ground}: the plans are drawn to the same scale and frame. Give it two corners only if its plan differs.

grid.hint_off: Turn it on to divide the field image into squares, with letters on the rows (A, B, …) and numbers on the columns (1, 2, …), for calling positions on the radio (“I'm in C4”).
grid.hint_on: The grid divides the image into equal parts and is drawn over it for everyone who sees the map (each viewer can hide it on their screen). Change the rows and columns and save.
grid.size: Each square is about {size} on the ground.
grid.bad: Rows go from 1 to {rows} and columns from 1 to {cols}.
grid.fm_toggle: Put a grid over the map
grid.fm_hint: Letters on the rows and numbers on the columns, for calling positions on the radio. It is saved with the field; you can change it later on the Field tab.
grid.print_foot: Call a position by its square: the row's letter, then the column's number (“C4”).
grid.print_webview: In the app on the phone, the grid map cannot be printed: open the console in a computer's browser for that.

features.title: Map features
features.intro: Mark safe zones, respawns, HQs, the car park, first aid and objectives on the plan, each as a pin, a circle or an area. Each one says who may see it: everyone, one team, or only the organisers.
features.intro_read: What is marked on the plan for you to see.
features.legend_team: A team's features are in the team's colour.
features.none: Nothing is marked on this plan yet.
features.label: Name (optional)
features.no_scale: The plan has no map position yet, so the circle is drawn at a set size, dashed. Give the plan its map position (below) to draw it to scale.
features.placing_point: Click the plan where it goes.
features.placing_circle: Press the plan at the centre and drag to the edge, or click the centre and type the radius.
features.placing_polygon: Click the plan at each corner of the area, in order ({n} so far, at least 3).
features.need_place: Place it on the plan first.
features.need_corners: An area needs at least 3 corners.
features.boundary_hint: The field boundary is an area, at most one per level and of no team; the plan is dimmed outside it.

beacons.title: Indoor beacons
beacons.intro: The Bluetooth beacons (iBeacon) you have put up in a building. A player's phone reports the strongest one it hears, and the room it is in is shown here and in ATAK. Room by room, not to the metre. Place each beacon on its level's plan to show the room on the map.
beacons.confirm_delete: Remove the beacon of {name}? Phones will no longer report it.
beacons.placing: Click the plan where the beacon is.
beacons.bad_uuid: The UUID is 32 hexadecimal digits, as 8-4-4-4-12.
beacons.bad_id: Major and minor are whole numbers from 0 to 65535.
beacons.boxes_intro: A Field Box joined to a game also advertises as an iBeacon, so a phone that hears it is placed in the room, on the floor, where you put the box on the plan above. Nothing to register: place the box and it appears here. You can disable one, or give it a room other than its name.
beacons.boxes_switch: The Field Boxes advertise as beacons (the boxes are told when the next game is joined)
beacons.boxes_none: No box is placed on a plan yet. Place a box on the field view above to make it a beacon.

map_fetching.title: Map fetching
map_fetching.intro: The page “Load the field from a map” asks OpenStreetMap, Overpass, Nominatim and the open aerial imagery services for the map and the field’s area, and sends them the IP address of the device that opens the page and the area asked for. Turn it off if the field does not want that: the page then stays closed and nothing leaves the controller. The field can still be loaded by uploading an image.
map_fetching.label: Let the console fetch maps from the internet

fieldmap.open: Load the field from a map
fieldmap.title: Load the field from a map
fieldmap.off: Map fetching is turned off for this field, so this page does not reach OpenStreetMap, Overpass, Nominatim or any aerial imagery service. To load the field from a map, the GM turns it on under Settings, “Map fetching”. You can also upload an image of the field on the Field tab.
fieldmap.off_note: Map fetching is off for this field (Settings).
fieldmap.login: Sign in to the console with the GM code first, then open this page from the Field tab.
fieldmap.intro: Find the field on the map and mark the corners of its outline: this browser draws the field image from open maps. The image, its place on the map (ATAK) and the field boundary are then saved on the field controller, which needs no internet for this.
fieldmap.sources: Only while you set the game up: this browser fetches the map and the area once, from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors) and, where there is one, the country's or region's open aerial imagery (the DGT orthophoto in mainland Portugal, IGN's PNOA in Spain, IGN's orthophotos in France and PDOK's in the Netherlands, and the public services' of Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland, eleven German states, Poland and Czechia, each with its credit). If OpenStreetMap's data service is busy, the same question (only the field's area) goes to another public server with the same data (overpass.private.coffee). Nothing else is downloaded, and the rest of the console keeps working without internet.
fieldmap.offline: This page needs internet, and this device has none now. The rest of the console works without it.
fieldmap.go: Search for a place, or go to “latitude, longitude”
fieldmap.locating: Asking this browser for your location…
fieldmap.located: The map is at your location (accurate to about {m} m).
fieldmap.restored: The outline you were drawing is back ({n} corners): carry on.
fieldmap.search_note: A place's name is sent to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim search only when you press Search (at most once a second); coordinates never leave this browser. Your location stays in this browser too: it is not sent to the field controller or anywhere else.
fieldmap.found: Places found: {n}. Choose one to move the map there.
fieldmap.not_found: No place found for “{q}”. Try another name, or type “latitude, longitude”.

place_errors.empty: Type a place's name, or “latitude, longitude”.
place_errors.busy_here: Still searching: wait for the answer.
place_errors.offline: No internet: place search needs it. Coordinates and your location work without it.
place_errors.refused: OpenStreetMap's place search refused or is busy ({detail}): try again in a while, or type “latitude, longitude”.
place_errors.failed: The place could not be searched for ({detail}).

locate_errors.insecure: Browsers give the location only to secure pages: open the console over https:// (the field's HTTPS address) or on this computer at 127.0.0.1 or localhost. Meanwhile, search for the place by name or type “latitude, longitude”.
locate_errors.unsupported: This browser does not give the location. Search for the place by name or type “latitude, longitude”.
locate_errors.denied: This page is not allowed your location. You can allow it in the browser's settings for this address, or search for the place by name.
locate_errors.unavailable: This device could not tell where it is right now. Try again, or search for the place by name.
locate_errors.timeout: Finding your location took too long. Try again (outdoors helps), or search for the place by name.

fieldmap.map_label: Map: drag to move, the wheel or + and − to zoom, press to mark a corner
fieldmap.map_help: Drag the map, or select it and use the arrow keys, to move it; + and − zoom in and out. Press the map at each corner of the field, in order; with the keyboard, put the cross on a corner and use “Add a corner at the cross”.
fieldmap.layer_none: Here there is only OpenStreetMap's map: open high-resolution aerial imagery that may be used is only available in mainland Portugal, Spain, France (with Corsica and its overseas territories), the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland and Liechtenstein, Poland, Czechia, and Germany except Baden-Württemberg, Lower Saxony, Hamburg, Saxony-Anhalt and Schleswig-Holstein.
fieldmap.add_centre: Add a corner at the cross
fieldmap.need_corners: The outline needs at least 3 corners.
fieldmap.label: Name of the boundary (optional)
fieldmap.cancelled: Cancelled: nothing more is asked of OpenStreetMap. You can draw again whenever you like.

busy.osm: Fetching OpenStreetMap's data for the area…
busy.osm_retry: OpenStreetMap's data service is busy: trying again in {s} s ({host})…
busy.osm_from: Fetching OpenStreetMap's data from {host} (try {n} of at most {max}), waiting for the answer…

fieldmap.preview_alt: The field image drawn from the map, with the outline
fieldmap.preview_next: Check the image and use “Use as the field” to save it on the field controller: until then nothing is saved.
fieldmap.ready: The field image is drawn, but not saved yet.
fieldmap.leave_confirm: The drawn field image has not been saved. Leave anyway and lose it?
fieldmap.source_both: The orthophoto ({name}) with OpenStreetMap's paths, buildings and names.
fieldmap.replaces: The field already has an image: this replaces it and its place on the map. The boxes and the map features keep their places on the image and may need moving.
fieldmap.replaces_level: {name} already has a plan: this replaces it and its place on the map. The boxes and the map features keep their places on the plan and may need moving.
fieldmap.done: Saved: the field image, its place on the map (ATAK) and the field boundary.
fieldmap.loaded: Field loaded from the map: the image, its place on the map (ATAK) and the field boundary are saved.
fieldmap.loaded_level: {name} loaded from the map: the plan, its place on the map (ATAK) and the field boundary are saved.
fieldmap.no_ortho: The orthophoto ({name}) has no picture of this area: the image is drawn from OpenStreetMap alone.
fieldmap.osm_from: OpenStreetMap's data came from {host} (the main server was busy); this server's data may be a few months old.
fieldmap.ortho_failed: The orthophoto ({name}) could not be fetched ({detail}): the image is drawn from OpenStreetMap alone.

errors.too_big: The outline is too big ({detail} across; at most 4 km): draw a smaller one.
errors.offline: No internet: this page needs it to fetch the map.
errors.busy: OpenStreetMap's data servers are busy ({detail}), even after several tries over about a minute: try again in a few minutes.
errors.too_much: Too much map data in this area: draw a smaller outline.
errors.osm_failed: OpenStreetMap's data could not be fetched ({detail}).
errors.ortho_failed: The orthophoto could not be fetched ({detail}).
errors.too_big_image: The image is still over 4 MB after making it smaller: draw a smaller outline.
errors.unreachable: OpenStreetMap's data servers could not be reached ({detail}): they are busy or unreachable. Check the internet connection, or try again in a few minutes.

join.title: Join boxes and controllers
join.intro: Make the join data for a box (NFC card or serial console) or for a standby controller. A standby controller's join also carries where the boxes are placed and the beacon choices (rooms, disabled boxes), so a promoted standby places players the same way: generate it again after you move or change a box.
join.warning: Careful: this code and the card carry the game key. Show them only to the people setting up the field.
join.qr_label: QR code with the join data
join.copy_failed: Could not copy: select the text and copy it by hand.
join.nfc_hint: Bytes to write to the card's memory from page 4 (NDEF message).
join.no_game: No game is running on this controller.
join.standby_intro: Paste the text the main controller made for a standby controller. Both controllers must share the same field join key.
join.standby_done: This controller is now on standby in game {game}.
join.gm_only: Only the organisers can make join data.
join.standby_cannot_issue: A standby controller does not make join data; use the controller in charge.
join.scenario_hint: The scenario finds its boxes by these names: {done} of {n} have a box.

scoreboard.title: Scoreboard
scoreboard.token_needed: Open the scoreboard with the read code in its address: …/scoreboard.html#token=CODE

radio.title: Field radio channel
radio.move_telling: Telling the free boxes on the old channel ({from} MHz) that the field is moving to {to} MHz: said {sent} of {repeats} times. This takes about 5 seconds; the controller moves when it is done.
radio.move_moved: The controller has moved to {to} MHz. Free boxes that heard the message follow it and announce themselves within about 15 seconds.
radio.find_boxes_hint: Asks the free boxes to announce themselves, and looks on the earlier channels for boxes that were away when the channel changed. Only between games.
radio.limits_conducted: {duty}% of the time · {mw} mW at the antenna port
radio.region_hint: Pick the region once, for the country the field is in. Only regions the boxes and the USB modem are built for work: a box built for another region refuses the joins.
radio.region_confirm: Move the field to {region}? Every box and the USB modem must be built for this region (their firmware refuses the others), and the channel goes back to the region's default until you choose one.
radio.region_mismatch: The USB modem is built for {modem}, but the field is in {field}: the modem refuses this region's channels, so no game can start. Use a modem built for {field}, or change the region back.
radio.why_tw_1: In Taiwan these devices may use 920–925 MHz (NCC LP0002). A transmitter that does not hop between channels must spread over at least 500 kHz, so the field's channel is 500 kHz wide (LoRa SF9, about the range of SF7 at 125 kHz elsewhere), at up to 0.5 W at the antenna port outdoors.
radio.why_tw_2: The recommended channel stays clear of 923.2 and 923.4 MHz, where every LoRaWAN device in Taiwan starts, and of Meshtastic's default (923.875 MHz).
radio.why_tw_3: The rules set no duty cycle; the boxes and the modem keep themselves to 10% of the time, as the game is designed for. The firmware is not certified for Taiwan yet: a product sold there needs NCC type approval.
radio.default_hint_tw: {channel} MHz: clear of LoRaWAN's and Meshtastic's busy channels (see above).
radio.random_hint_tw: Draws one of the candidate 500 kHz channels; every one allows the full 0.5 W.
radio.not_chosen: not chosen yet: the recommended one applies
radio.low_power_warning: This channel allows only 25 mW and about a tenth of the recommended channel's airtime: less range, and with many boxes their transmissions may run out of allowed time.
radio.first_setup: Before the first game, choose the field's radio channel. Until then it is {channel} MHz, the recommended one.
radio.why_1: It is the centre of 869.4–869.65 MHz, the only part of the European 868 MHz band where a device may transmit up to 10% of the time at up to 500 mW (ERP). Everywhere else in 868–870 MHz the rules allow 1% of the time (0.1% on 868.7–869.2 MHz) at 25 mW: about a tenth of the airtime, and much less range.
radio.why_2: 868.1, 868.3 and 868.5 MHz are the channels every LoRaWAN device in Europe starts on, so they are often busy.
radio.why_3: The recommended channel is shared: LoRaWAN gateways send some of their replies on 869.525 MHz, and Meshtastic's European default is the same frequency. Their packets are not mistaken for the game's (the game's are encrypted and use another sync word), but every transmission nearby uses the same airtime. If such users are near the field, a scan shows whether another channel is quieter.
radio.locked_game: A game is live: end it to change the channel.
radio.default_hint: {channel} MHz: the most airtime and power European rules allow (see above).
radio.scan_hint: The USB modem listens to each candidate channel, about {seconds} s in all, without transmitting, and lists them quietest first. Nothing changes until you accept.

unavailable.no_modem: No USB modem is configured, so there is no radio to measure the noise with. The channel stays as it is.
unavailable.modem_down: The USB modem is not connected; the scan needs it.
unavailable.no_radio: The USB modem has no radio chip, so it cannot measure the noise.
unavailable.old_firmware: The USB modem's firmware cannot measure noise: update it.

suggest.quiet_full_power: Suggested: {channel} MHz, the quietest full-power channel ({limits}).
suggest.quietest: Suggested: {channel} MHz, the quietest channel ({limits}). The 500 mW channels were noisier.
suggest.quietest_but_noisy: Every channel is noisy. The least noisy is {channel} MHz ({limits}).

radio.results_caption: Quietest first. Quiet: 90% of the readings at {threshold} dBm or lower, and little LoRa activity.
radio.random_hint: Draws one of the candidate channels. It will usually be a 1%, 25 mW channel; only 869.475, 869.525 and 869.575 MHz give 10% and 500 mW.
radio.low_airtime_warning: 0.1% of the time: about 3.6 s of transmission per hour for each device, too little for a game.
radio.read_only: Only the organisers can change the channel.

glyphs.none: The boxes cannot draw {letters}: a mode's screen shows “?” for it and the box's own screens an empty square. The app and this console show the name as typed; on the box, teams are told apart by colour.
glyphs.some: {letters} is in only some of the box's text sizes, so a box may show “?” for it on part of its screens.

checkin_import.title: Import a registration list
checkin_import.intro: For a field with no site server: a list of registrations from another platform (CSV or JSON, the site server's import format) becomes this game's expected players, and a marshal ticks each one when they arrive. Only display_name, external_ref, team_preference, federation_number and replicas are read; any other column (an email, a phone number) is only named, never read.
checkin_import.file: File (CSV or JSON, up to 1 MiB, UTF-8)
checkin_import.source_hint: The other platform's name (a-z, 0-9, dot, dash, underscore). The same source and external_ref update the same player.
checkin_import.basis: This field is responsible for the list: it has its own legal basis for holding these players' data.
checkin_import.order: Check first: nothing is changed until Import.
checkin_import.counts: {rows} rows: {created} new, {updated} changed, {unchanged} unchanged, {skipped} skipped, {refused} refused.
checkin_import.missing: {n} imported players that have not arrived are not in this file (they stay).

codes.encoding_invalid: the file is not UTF-8 text
codes.json_invalid: not valid JSON (an array of objects)
codes.format_invalid: not a CSV or JSON file
codes.source_invalid: the source is not valid (a-z, 0-9, dot, dash, underscore; not "site")
codes.basis_not_confirmed: confirm that this field has its own basis for the list
codes.row_length: the row does not have as many cells as the header
codes.display_name_invalid: name missing or not 1-32 characters on one line
codes.team_preference_invalid: not a team of this game
codes.federation_number_required: this field asks for the number
codes.replicas_not_asked: this game does not take declared replicas
codes.too_many_replicas: more replicas than the field allows
codes.replica_class_invalid: replica class not in the field's limits
codes.no_external_ref: no external_ref: added again each time
codes.federation_number_dropped: number not kept: this field asks for none

checkin.title: Field check-in
checkin.intro: Players scan the field's poster with the app, check in and declare the replicas they will use in this game. Names are shown only here and in the marshals' view.
checkin.print_labels_all: Print labels for everyone checked in
checkin.webview_notice: In the app on the phone, the poster cannot be printed and the CSV cannot be saved: open the console in a computer's browser for that.
checkin.empty: Nobody has checked in to this game yet.
checkin.name: Name

marshals.title: Marshals
marshals.intro: Only people on this list can act as marshals. Add a player who has checked in: the controller gives them an id (M-01, M-02...) and the marshal role, and their app shows "you are marshal M-01" once it has confirmed with this controller. Taking someone off the list stops them at once.
marshals.empty: No marshals yet. Add a player who has checked in.
marshals.name: Name
marshals.add_id: Id (made by the controller if left empty; give the old one to put someone back)
marshals.add_name: Name (the player's own if left empty)
marshals.remove_confirm: Take {id} ({name}) off the marshal list? Their app stops being a marshal at once, and readings they have not sent yet are refused until you add them again.

checkin.number_erased: number erased after the card check
checkin.share_position: Share my position with the game during this game
checkin.share_position_hint: Separate and unticked unless the player agrees. Their squad or team (as the mode allows), the marshals and the GM see it; the remote GM only if the field turns that on. Saying no changes nothing else. They can stop at any time.
checkin.card_why: The field must check the physical card against the data typed in advance (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR for fields in Portugal, Art. 6(1)(f) elsewhere).
checkin.manual_hint: For players without the app: the controller makes their id, which can be written to a player tag.
checkin.valid_day: A pass counts for the rest of the day at this field.
checkin.valid_game: Every game asks for a new chronograph.
checkin.unregistered: not registered at the field yet
checkin.confirm_staff: by the GM or a marshal
checkin.federation_note: The number is never verified automatically. Where the field’s APD rule checks at check-in, a player stays pending until you compare the physical card with what they typed and tick “card seen, matches”; the number is then erased and the result, the date and your id are kept.
checkin.apd_checkin: Check the player's APD membership at check-in
checkin.apd_expiry: Ask for the expiry date and check it
checkin.apd_no_list: The project's list of APDs is empty for now: add your own below.
checkin.apd_custom: Add an APD of your own
checkin.apd_custom_hint: For an APD the project's list does not have yet. It is kept on this controller and sent to the players' apps.
checkin.apd_note: Nothing is verified automatically: players declare their APD, number and expiry and the marshal sees a verdict. A check-in the rule does not accept waits for a marshal, who can always confirm it; that is logged.
checkin.country_hint: PT shows the APD texts. Any other country (or none) says association membership and the list offers that country's associations. Empty: PT where the time zone is Portugal's.
checkin.apd_checkin_m: Check the player's association membership at check-in
checkin.apd_no_list_m: The project's list has no associations for this country yet: add your own below.
checkin.apd_custom_m: Add an association of your own
checkin.apd_custom_hint_m: For an association the project's list does not have (a club, federation or insurance body). It is kept on this controller and sent to the players' apps.
checkin.apd_note_m: Nothing is verified automatically: players declare their association, number and expiry and the marshal sees a verdict. A check-in the rule does not accept waits for a marshal, who can always confirm it; that is logged.
checkin.poster_intro: Print it once and put it up in the check-in area: it serves every game at the field. It holds no key and no password.
checkin.poster_urls: The controller's https addresses (one per line)
checkin.no_game: No game is live: create one to open check-in. The poster can be printed now.
checkin.ticket_hint: Scan or paste the code of a registered player's printed ticket (atalaia:ticket:…).
checkin.schedule_intro: The site server's published games of the coming days. A game made from one takes its title, mode and teams; its registered players then appear here as expected.

problems.https_off: HTTPS is off on the controller ([api] tls_port = 0): the poster needs the field's certificate.
problems.no_address: The poster has no https address for the controller: set the addresses below, [checkin] urls or [api] tls_names.
problems.too_long: The poster does not fit in a QR code: fewer or shorter addresses, or a shorter field name.

checkin.schedule_none: No scheduled games pulled from the site server yet.

poster.title: Check-in poster
poster.login: Open the console with the GM token first.
poster.no_text: The poster cannot be made yet.
poster.qr_label: QR code for checking in at the field
poster.intro: Print this page on A4. The code holds no secrets: it can stay in plain view.
poster.wifi_label: QR code for the Wi-Fi network
poster.wifi_note: The password is used only to draw the Wi-Fi code: it is neither kept nor sent.

labels.title: Replica labels
labels.login: Open the console with the GM token first.
labels.none: Nobody checked in has declared a replica yet.
labels.intro: Print this page: one label of 30 × 30 mm for each replica, to cut out and stick on. The code holds only the replica's label (ATL- and eight characters), nothing about the player. The marshal's app scans it in the chrono queue.

branding.from_site_hint: The field's name, accent colour, logo and wallpaper come from the site server and change there; this controller takes them at its next sync.
branding.title: Field branding
branding.intro: How players see this field: its name, logo, wallpaper and colour, in the app, on the scoreboard, on the check-in poster and in this console. Anyone on the field's network can see them; they hold no personal data.
branding.field_name_hint: Also printed on the check-in poster.
branding.accent_hint: On the app's main buttons and this console's header.
branding.limits: PNG, JPEG or WebP (no SVG). Logo up to 1 MB and 2048 px a side, wallpaper up to 4 MB and 4096 px a side. Metadata such as the camera or where a photo was taken is removed.
branding.rights: Upload only images you have the right to use (your field's or club's own, or with the owner's permission): you are responsible for them.
branding.bad_type: The image must be PNG, JPEG or WebP.
branding.read_only: Only the GM can change the field's branding.

teams.site_hint: The field's saved teams come from the site server and change there: they cannot be edited or deleted here. Crests and colours reach this controller at its next sync.
teams.title: Saved teams
teams.intro: Teams that come back: a name and a crest to pick when you create a game. The colour stays the team's colour on the boxes and buttons.
teams.name: Team name
teams.crest_limits: PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 512 KB and 1024 px a side.
teams.for_game_hint: Optional: a name and a crest for each team colour, shown to players, on the scoreboard and on Android props. The boxes keep showing the colour.

scenario.title: Scenario editor
scenario.intro: A scenario is a YAML manifest: the boxes the GM names, and the objectives (capture, code, tags, bomb, escort, defend, survive). The controller checks it as you type; once installed, create a game of it with Objectives in the Game tab.
scenario.ok: No problems: the generated field.lua loads in the core.
scenario.ok_no_core: No problems in the manifest (the core is not loaded on this controller).
scenario.nodes_hint: In the Join tab, give each of these names to a box.
scenario.player_node: a player whose check-in role is {role}
scenario.name: Name
scenario.game_hint: A game of a scenario: in the Game tab, pick the scenario and tick Objectives.
scenario.read_only: The read-only code checks only: installing is the GM's.

scenario_blocks.intro: The same manifest as blocks. Each change to the blocks writes the YAML again (its comments go), and the controller checks it as before. Add blocks from the categories; the YAML view shows the text.
scenario_blocks.keyboard: Keyboard: Tab reaches the categories; the arrow keys go from item to item (right: into a category's blocks or a block's fields); Enter takes a block (the arrows choose where, Enter puts it down) or edits a field; W goes to the blocks, T to the categories, M moves a block, Delete removes it, Ctrl+Z undoes.
scenario_blocks.cannot_read: This text is not a manifest the blocks can show: fix it in the YAML view first (the checks below say why).
scenario_blocks.lost: The blocks cannot show these parts as they are: {paths}. Change them in the YAML view first.
scenario_blocks.no_controller: The controller did not answer: the blocks need it to read the YAML.

problems.loose: This block is not part of the scenario: put it inside or delete it.
problems.misplaced: This block does not go here.
problems.twice: Given twice: only the first one counts.

blocks.scenario_lang: boxes' screens in %1 squads per team %2
blocks.scenario_rules: objectives are known %1 and told to %2
blocks.scenario_tip: The scenario: its id (your club's, like org.club.foxhound), version and name; the language of the boxes' screens; its teams, parameters, boxes and objectives.
blocks.author: author %1
blocks.param: parameter %1 whole number from %2 to %3 default %4
blocks.param_tip: A number the GM can change when creating the game, for "gives the points of parameter". Leave from and to empty for 0 and 100000.
blocks.box_tip: A box the GM gives this name in the Join tab. Level: the floor it goes on, on a multi-story field.
blocks.player_tip: A checked-in player with this role (the VIP of an escort).
blocks.objective_tip: An objective: its id (a-z, 0-9 and _), its name, its type and the box or player it targets (survive has none). Inside: who, when, how and what it gives.
blocks.area: destination: the area with the corners %1

firmware.title: Firmware updates
firmware.hint: Upload a signed release (the image and its .release.json), then update the boxes before the game starts. Each box checks the signature again with its own keys and installs over the field Wi-Fi; if the new firmware does not start properly, the box goes back to the previous one.
firmware.no_keys: No release key is configured on this controller ([firmware] release_keys): no release is accepted.
firmware.no_https: This controller does not serve HTTPS: boxes download updates only over HTTPS, checked against the field's certificate.
firmware.not_ready: Updates go out only while the live game has not started: create a game, join the boxes and update them before you start it.
firmware.bad_release_file: The .release.json file could not be read.
firmware.send_again_hint: The box has not answered yet: send the update again now (a box already updating ignores it)
firmware.cancel: Stop waiting for the updates on their way

reasons.no_key: no release key in the box's firmware
reasons.no_link: the box's join has no field certificate or address
reasons.no_wifi: no field Wi-Fi on the box
reasons.unreachable: the box could not reach the controller
reasons.bad_signature: the signature did not verify on the box
reasons.layout: needs a newer partition table: USB flash required once
reasons.bad_hash: the image was not the signed one
reasons.self_test: the new firmware failed its self-test
reasons.radio_duty_cycle: the radio's airtime budget was spent: send it again in a few minutes
reasons.radio_queue_full: the radio's queue was full: send it again
reasons.radio_failed: the radio did not send the offer

results.in_progress: an update is already on its way

adopt.title: Adopt boxes
adopt.intro: A new box is adopted once by this field: it then holds the field join key and takes this field's join cards. A box adopted by another field (or to this field's old key) moves only with its admin PIN.
adopt.previous: The field join key was rotated; boxes still on the old key ({field}) need their admin PIN to be adopted again.
adopt.gm_only: Only the organisers can adopt boxes.
adopt.usb_intro: Plug the new box into this controller by USB and look for it. Check its name and MAC (the box shows them on its serial console; the MAC is also on its USB port's serial number) before you adopt it.
adopt.usb_off: USB adoption is off on this controller ([adopt] usb = false).
adopt.none: No box found. Check the cable (a data cable, not only power) and that the box is switched on.
adopt.busy: a game is joined: end it first
adopt.locked: too many wrong PINs: wait {min} min (a restart does not shorten it)
adopt.confirm_hint: The controller checks it is still that box before it writes the key.
adopt.pin_hint: This box belongs to another field (or to this field's old key): its admin PIN is needed. After five wrong PINs in a row each try waits 1, 2, 4… up to 60 minutes, also after the box restarts.

state.previous_key: adopted to this field's old key ({field})

result.same: Box {name} ({mac}) was already adopted by this field.
result.need_pin: Box {name} belongs to another field: type its admin PIN.
result.locked: Box {name}: too many wrong PINs; try again when the box says so (up to 60 minutes).
result.no_pin: Box {name} belongs to another field and has no admin PIN: set one on the box's USB console ("@admin-pin").
result.busy: Box {name} has a game joined: end the game first.
result.bad_card: A damaged field card was tapped.
result.store_failed: Box {name} could not store the key.
result.channel_changed: the radio left the pairing channel during {name}'s run

adopt.card_intro: Write these bytes on an NTAG215 or NTAG216 card, as a join card, and tap it once on each new box. A box adopted by another field asks for its admin PIN on the keypad.
adopt.card_warning: This card is the field's master secret: it holds the field join key. Whoever has it can make join cards for this field's boxes and read the keys of later games sent over the radio. Keep it locked away, never give it to players, and make as few as you need.
adopt.card_hint: Bytes to write to the card's memory from page 4 (NDEF message, type application/vnd.atalaia.field).
adopt.card_lost: A field card lost or copied? Rotate the key on the controller (python3 -m atalaia_controller join-key --rotate), restart it, adopt every box again and destroy the old cards.
adopt.code_intro: An unadopted box shows a 6-digit code when it starts. Look for boxes on the radio, pick it by its name, and type the code it shows: the box gets this field's key over the radio, sealed, without a cable or a card. A wrong code changes the box's code; three wrong ones make it wait a minute.
adopt.code_listen: Look for boxes on the radio
adopt.code_channel: Listening on {mhz} MHz, where new boxes listen, for five minutes.
adopt.code_none: No box is offering itself yet. Check that its screen shows a code ("@pair" or a restart shows a new one).

code_run.sealing: Pairing {name}: the code matched, sending the key…

code_why.wrong_code: the code was not the one the box shows. Read its screen again: a real box now shows a new code; if its code did not change, this entry was not your box.
code_why.no_answer: no answer: out of range, the code no longer on its screen, or another pairing under way with it (radio interference); try again.
code_why.no_done: it did not confirm; look at its screen.
code_why.fingerprint: it holds another key than this field's.
code_why.duty_cycle: the radio's duty cycle is used up for now.
code_why.channel_changed: the radio left the pairing channel (the region's default: 869.525 MHz in Europe, 921.5 MHz in Taiwan) for the field's channel, a scan or the modem reconnecting; look for boxes again.

adopt.code_duplicate: More than one box offers itself under this name: type the code only into the entry whose id is the one on the box's screen.

poster_prompt.title: Print the check-in poster?
poster_prompt.body: Players check in by scanning the field's poster. If it is not up yet, print it before they arrive for “{game}”. It is the same for every game.
poster_prompt.announce: This message closes by itself in {n} seconds.
poster_prompt.setting: Suggest printing the check-in poster after a game is created
poster_prompt.paused: Paused: it stays open until you close it

invites.title: Boxes for this game
invites.intro: Boxes whose game is over announce themselves over the radio. Tick the ones for this game: the controller sends each one its join over the radio, encrypted with the field's key.
invites.discover_sent: Asked the free boxes to announce themselves.
invites.discover_recent: The free boxes were asked a moment ago; waiting for their answers.
invites.discover_sweep: Also looked on the earlier channels: {channels} MHz. Boxes there are told to move; answers can take up to 30 seconds.
invites.discover_capped: No sweep of the earlier channels: on a {duty}% channel the radio may use only {share}% of an hour's air time for sweeps, and that is used up for now. The next sweep is possible in {minutes} min.
invites.discover_never: No sweep of the earlier channels: a {duty}% channel has too little air time for a sweep.
invites.missing_help: A box that is still missing after this must be adopted again (Adopt tab) or be near the controller, switched on and free, during the next channel change.
invites.empty: No free box heard yet. A box announces itself up to 20 s after its game ends (its screen says “Ready”), then about once a minute; “Look for boxes” asks them now.
invites.no_radio: The radio modem is not connected: boxes can be neither heard nor invited.
invites.old_modem: The radio modem's firmware does not carry field frames: update it.
invites.manual: Join cards, QR codes and the serial console work as before (Join tab).

reasons.no_mode: the mode is not on the box
reasons.storage: the box could not store it
reasons.radio: the box's radio may not transmit
reasons.ended: it has played that game already

invites.ready: Ready to start: every role has a box ({counts}). You can close this dialog.
invites.waiting: Still waiting for a box for: {roles}. Joined so far: {counts}.
invites.no_roles: This game needs no box to start. You can close this dialog.
invites.start_question: Review the game's other settings first?

box_language.title: Box language
box_language.intro: The language of the box screens: Ready, waiting for the start, neutral zone, armed, game over. A game keeps the language it was created with, and every join (card, QR code, text, radio invite) carries it. Boxes with older firmware stay in English.
box_language.label: Language on the boxes

choices.auto: This console's language when the game is created

box_language.saved: Saved: games created from now on use it.
box_language.read_only: Only the game master changes it.

packages.title: Signed mode packages
packages.hint: Install a mode signed with one of this controller's mode keys: upload its archive and .release.json (tools/mode_package.py), or take it from the field's registry index. The controller checks the signature, the archive and the scripts before it installs anything.
packages.no_keys: No mode key is configured on this controller ([modes] keys): no signed package is installed.
packages.bad_release_file: The .release.json file could not be read.
packages.none_installed: No mode installed besides the built-in ones.

trust.untrusted: its key is no longer trusted here

packages.no_index: No registry index is configured ([modes] index: an https:// address, or an index.json with its packages next to it).
packages.index_error: The index could not be read, so nothing is offered from it: {error}

states.no_key: signed with a key this controller does not trust
states.builtin: a built-in mode has this id

mode_fetch.send_hint: Invites the box again: it fetches the signed packages it lacks from this controller over the field Wi-Fi (HTTPS), checks them with the keys in its own firmware, and only then joins.

why.no_box_keys: no box mode keys are set on this controller ([modes] box_keys)
why.no_https: this controller does not serve HTTPS, and boxes fetch modes only over HTTPS
why.firmware: every part is built in, so this box's firmware is older than the game: update it (Boxes tab)
why.tier: a part needs a Full box
why.other: upload the part as a package signed with a key built into the boxes' firmware (Presets tab)

parts.missing: not on this controller: upload it
parts.unsigned: not signed: upload it as a signed package
parts.untrusted: its key is no longer trusted here
parts.no_box_key: not signed with a key built into the boxes
parts.too_big: too big for a box (over 256 KiB)

states.fetching: fetching its missing modes over Wi-Fi
states.hello_seen: said HELLO without reporting its modes: waiting for its news

reasons.no_mode: its firmware cannot fetch modes (older, or no mode key built in): update its firmware
reasons.no_wifi: no Wi-Fi: set the field's Wi-Fi on the box
reasons.unreachable: it could not reach this controller over HTTPS
reasons.not_offered: this controller no longer offers it
reasons.no_key: no mode key is built into the box
reasons.bad_release: the signed release is not valid
reasons.bad_signature: not signed with a key built into the box
reasons.kind: a box does not run this kind
reasons.builtin: the box has a built-in mode with that id
reasons.bad_hash: the package is not the one that was signed
reasons.load: the script does not load on the box
reasons.no_space: no room left on the box
reasons.storage: the box could not store it
reasons.report_lost: it said HELLO, but no report that it keeps every part came

mode_fetch.waiting: The game waits for boxes fetching modes (at most {s} s).
mode_fetch.boxes_hint: Boxes keep the signed modes they fetched for a game (at most 8, 512 KiB in all). A box marked here forgets them at its next invite; a factory reset forgets them too.
mode_fetch.box_keys: Mode keys built into the boxes ([modes] box_keys):
mode_fetch.no_box_keys: No box mode keys are set ([modes] box_keys): no mode can be sent to a box.
mode_fetch.none: No box has reported fetched modes yet.
mode_fetch.will_forget: Forgets them at its next invite

areas.branding: the field's branding and team crests

remote_gm.title: Remote GM log
remote_gm.intro: A person with the GM role on the site server can run the live game from afar when the remote GM is on in this controller's site settings. Every command they send is listed here, carried out or refused.
remote_gm.off: The remote GM is off on this controller: commands from the site server are refused. Turn it on in the controller's site settings.
remote_gm.failed: The log could not be read just now. Trying again.

scoreboard_share.title: Share the scoreboard with players
scoreboard_share.intro: Players scan this QR code with the app (Player > Follow a game without checking in) to see the time, the points and the events of the game on their phones. The code only lets them watch: it changes nothing.
scoreboard_share.none: This controller has no address to give yet: see the check-in poster's addresses.
scoreboard_share.qr_label: QR code of the scoreboard's address with the read-only access code
scoreboard_share.warning: The code in this QR code is the read-only access code: whoever has it can follow every game on this field. Show it to players on the field only; do not print it or post it online.

poster_changed.title: The poster changed.
poster_changed.ca: The field's certificate changed since the poster was printed: printed posters no longer work.
poster_changed.gone: The controller's addresses changed since the poster was printed (now: {now}): the printed poster no longer reaches it.
poster_changed.partly: The controller's addresses changed since the poster was printed (gone: {gone}; new: {now}): the printed one still works through the addresses it shares.
poster_changed.alert: The check-in poster changed, print it again. {what}

tags.title: Players' tags
tags.intro: Some modes need an NFC tag for each player. The controller signs each tag with this game's key, which never leaves it, so the tag works only in this game and only its boxes accept it.
tags.game: Game {game}: a new game needs new tags.
tags.player_hint: Letters, digits, - _ and . (up to 32), e.g. p-17. Pick a player who has checked in, or type an id.
tags.nfc_write: Write it with this device's NFC
tags.nfc_hold: Hold a blank tag to the back of this device…
tags.nfc_unsupported: This browser cannot write NFC tags (Web NFC needs Chrome on Android, over HTTPS). Write the bytes below with the Atalaia app (Marshal, Players' tags; on a phone controller, its own screen), or with an NFC app that can write a raw NDEF record from hex.
tags.no_game: Make a game first: tags are signed with the running game's key.

pod_config.title: I/O pods' settings
pod_config.hint: Sets the buttons' colours, the ring's brightness, the volume and the enclosure switch of the I/O pod a phone is linked to, over the radio, sealed with the game key. Only the settings you fill in change; the pod keeps them in its flash. Radio, pins and Bluetooth security stay as built.
pod_config.not_ready: Pod settings go out only before a game starts or after it ended.
pod_config.no_phones: No phone has said hello in this game yet: join the phone that has the pod first.
pod_config.reset: Back to the build's settings first
pod_config.no_answer_hint: No answer: the phone has no I/O pod, the pod's firmware is older than this feature, or it is out of radio reach. Sent again several times already.

retention.hint: 30 to 3653 days. Chrono readings (also other fields' copies) and marshals' earlier keys are deleted after the first; an ended game's events, scores and nodes after the second. With a site server connected, a game is never deleted before the site server has all of it. Both are the site server's when the field takes its settings from it.

projected_score.label: estimated {n}
projected_score.explain: Between the boxes' reports (every 15 s) the estimate adds the points a held box has made since, for modes that say how they score. Only the number without "estimated" is the official score.

objective_reveal.label: Objectives at the start
objective_reveal.default: As the scenario says; in a game with squads, only the active ones
objective_reveal.active: Only the active ones; the next is revealed when it opens
objective_reveal.hint: For the objectives that depend on others and say nothing about it themselves. An objective's own setting in the scenario always wins. Fixed when the game is made.
objective_reveal.live_active: only the active ones are shown
